actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 410 - 1 (Roll no. 64). (text: CR H1051)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 410 - 1 (Roll no. 64). (text: CR H1051)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H1058-1059)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 901.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H1051-1052)
Mr. Green (TN) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Referred to the Subcommittee on Emergency Management and Technology.
Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects DHS officials, researchers involved in DHS-funded acquisitions, and GAO evaluators.
dimensions.evidence: Under Secretary of the Science and Technology Directorate of the Department of Homeland Security to develop a Department-wide policy

dimensions.assessment: Establishes internal agency security policies, oversight reporting, and briefings rather than direct public mandates.
dimensions.evidence: develop a department-wide policy for safeguarding research and development from unauthorized access

dimensions.assessment: Involves government-funded research and development security compliance, but does not specify new appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: certain disclosures about government-funded research and development

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to add research safeguarding duties and orders a GAO report on NSPM-33 compliance.
dimensions.evidence: Section 302 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 182) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Combines a permanent agency policy requirement with one-time or short-term reporting mandates (GAO report within one year, briefing within 90 days).
dimensions.evidence: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General... shall submit... a report

missing_information: Specific resources or personnel required to implement the department-wide research security policy.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Department of Homeland Security to develop a department-wide policy safeguarding research and development, and mandates a GAO compliance report and congressional briefing.
